title: `sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression` is removed and metrics-endpoint compression is on by default
quote: The annotation `sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression` was deprecated and removed. There now is the `statsCompression` option in proxyConfig to globally control compression support of the metrics endpoint
remediation: Drop the annotation from the listed pods; compression is now negotiated with the scraper's Accept-Encoding. To disable it per pod set `statsCompression: false` in the `proxy.istio.io/config` annotation, or globally in `meshConfig.defaultConfig`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations // {} | keys[] | startswith("sidecar.istio.io/statsCompression")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed pod carries the annotation 1.29 no longer reads

title: Ambient dry-run AuthorizationPolicies: enabling the new ztunnel support while old ztunnels remain makes them ENFORCE the dry-run policies

detection.reason: names the dry-run AuthorizationPolicies; whether the istiod flag is set is stated by the verify command

gate.reason: only an ambient (ztunnel) data plane is affected; a sidecar-only mesh has nothing to do

quote: Setting `AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY=true` will cause istiod to begin sending dry-run policies to ztunnel, using a new field in xDS. A ztunnel below version 1.29 will not support this field. As a result, older ztunnels will fully enforce these policies
remediation: Upgrade every ztunnel to 1.29 before setting `AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY=true` on istiod; until then leave the flag unset (istiod keeps withholding dry-run policies from ztunnel). The listed policies are the ones an old ztunnel would enforce.
verifyCommand: kubectl get authorizationpolicies.security.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["istio.io/dry-run"] == "true") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each printed dry-run policy is enforced by a pre-1.29 ztunnel if AMBIENT_ENABLE_DRY_RUN_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY is turned on early

title: istiod debug endpoints now require authorization — Kiali and custom tooling in non-system namespaces are restricted

detection.reason: which tools call istiod's debug endpoints is not on the cluster; a Kiali Deployment is the known candidate

quote: Tools accessing debug endpoints from non-system namespaces (such as Kiali or custom monitoring tools) may be affected. Non-system namespaces are now restricted to config_dump, ndsz, and edsz endpoints for same-namespace proxies only.
remediation: Run Kiali (and any tool that reads istiod `/debug/*`) in the Istio root namespace, upgrade it to a release that copes with the restriction, or set `ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH=false` on istiod to restore the old access.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("kiali/kiali"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image'  # a printed Kiali outside the Istio root namespace loses most debug endpoints at 1.29 unless ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH=false

title: Circuit-breaker `remaining_*` metrics are no longer tracked by default

detection.reason: which dashboards read the remaining_* series is not on the cluster; DestinationRules with connection-pool limits are the population whose metrics change

quote: Previously, these metrics were tracked by default. Now, tracking is disabled by default for better proxy memory usage.
remediation: Dashboards or alerts on `envoy_cluster_circuit_breakers_*_remaining_*` go empty after upgrade. Set `DISABLE_TRACK_REMAINING_CB_METRICS=false` on istiod (or use the compatibility version) to keep them; the DestinationRules with a `connectionPool` are where the limits being tracked are defined.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(DISABLE_TRACK_REMAINING_CB_METRICS)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # no printed line means remaining_* circuit-breaker metrics stop after upgrade

title: istio-cni now reconciles in-pod iptables rules of existing ambient pods on startup by default

detection.reason: a node-agent default; the istio-cni DaemonSet is the subject

quote: Iptables reconciliation is now enabled by default for ambient workloads in release 1.29.0. When a new `istio-cni` DaemonSet pod starts up, it will automatically inspect pods that were previously enrolled in the ambient mesh and upgrade their in-pod iptables/nftables rules
remediation: No action expected: after the istio-cni upgrade, already-enrolled ambient pods get their redirection rules brought up to date without a restart. Set `--set cni.ambient.reconcileIptablesOnStartup=false` to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/install-cni"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("RECONCILE")) | .name + "=" + (.value // "")] | join(","))'  # no reconcile setting printed means the 1.29 default (on) applies
